text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — compaction/evict ordering vs per-tenant SLOs. Found some production surprises this morning: compactor started during high qps and we saw 30-50ms p99 token latency spikes. Need to agree on ordering and backpressure.

aj: ugh. do we have traces?

maria: yes, debug trace link: https://internal/trace/abc123 :point_up:

kevin: main issue looks like compaction preempting hot-page evictions; compactor took IO bandwidth and stalled async page fetches.

tim: timeline? was compaction started by Scheduler or by in-heap idle-trigger?

maria: scheduler. policy was 'compact-on-idle' but idle detection incorrectly considered small-batch tail as idle. we should tighten thresholds.

sylvia: proposal: prioritize eviction work over compaction when memory pressure > 70% and have compaction only run on maintenance lanes. Also expose a tenant-level compaction throttle.

aj: agree. we also need backpressure signal from compactor -> request routing to avoid adding token work when compaction is in progress.

kevin: +1. suggest adding compaction_inprogress metric and SLO circuit to route new requests to warm model variant (lower memory) when compaction_inprogress == 1 && p99_latency > threshold

maria: rough config prototype:

```
compaction:
  mode: maintenance
  max_io_mb_per_sec: 100
  preempt_threshold_percent: 70
  tenant_throttle:
    enabled: true
    qps_limit_pct: 20
```

tim: nice. can we also favor small compactions (per-arena) vs global compaction? global is too disruptive.

sylvia: yes, plus we should coordinate with evictor: evictor should be able to "lease" IO tokens and compactor yields when evictor needs them.

aj: how do we test this? e2e simulation with mixed small/big batch traces + injected compaction schedule. need regression alert if p99 increases > 10%.

maria: I'll open an RFC follow-up with a draft API for compaction control and metrics. tagging infra-bot to create test job.

infra-bot: perf-ci job queued: scheduler/compaction-slo-sim (run id: 2026-03-23_01)

kevin: thanks. quick follow: migration path for current clusters? can we roll config change via canary first?

maria: yes. canary 5% with compaction.mode=maintenance and tenant_throttle on. monitor compaction_inprogress and p99_latency.

aj: sounds good. i'll pair with you on the RFC doc.

sylvia: :thumbsup: 

maria: thanks everyone, will post RFC link in #eng-runtime when ready.
